merge_frontal_prefrontal.reason: Parker's margin comment on idx 104 (TABLE 6-10): 'I don't want two flashcards talking about the prefrontal area because I highlighted both areas.' Cards 94 and 98 both clozed 'judgment' - exactly the redundancy he named. Merged into ONE note covering the frontal region once, with each region's duties tested under its own cloze number and both region names visible as anchors. The two-way (function->name) direction is deliberately dropped here because hiding 'frontal lobe' while 'prefrontal' stays visible would leak the answer; card 93 still tests the four lobe names. Grounding check: 'prefrontal' appears ONLY inside the TABLE 6-10 image, never in the chapter text, so the card does NOT assert that the prefrontal area sits inside the frontal lobe (unstated in source).
merge_frontal_prefrontal.revised_Text: The frontal lobe governs {{c1::personality}}, {{c1::planning}}, {{c1::problem solving}}, {{c1::concentration}}, {{c1::self-awareness}}, and {{c1::voluntary muscle control}}, while the prefrontal area handles {{c2::judgment}}, {{c2::predicting the consequences of actions}}, and {{c2::abstract intellectual functions}}.
merge_frontal_prefrontal.revised_Back_Extra:
Distinguish: the chapter's own text credits judgment to the frontal lobe broadly, while the prefrontal area is the region named for it precisely.

Cue: the frontal lobe also stores the memories of the voluntary movements it controls.
